thread:
ori: Customer escalation — on-prem app hitting Redwood via PrivateLink intermittently 401 / TLS resets. Works from some offices but many customer subnets fail. Logs show TLS handshake failures and occasional 401. Can we collect quick repro + next steps?
anya: Thanks ori. Ticket #12345 created. Can you confirm which endpoint type (Interface VPCE / NLB) and region, and paste a curl + trace from an affected host?
sam: Quick thought: do they have an outbound proxy or HTTPS-inspecting firewall? If a proxy terminates TLS or rewrites Host/SNI, that will break our cert validation or routing.
customer-engineer: They confirmed corporate proxy on some subnets. Most traffic should NAT out via a NAT-GW, but some hosts are forced through proxy. Proxy injects Proxy-Authorization header and rewrites Host for their internal routing.
mike: That explains TLS resets. If proxy performs TLS interception, the client never sees Redwood cert/SNI. On PrivateLink we rely on TLS passthrough to the endpoint; proxy MITM will break the handshake and can result in 401 if it rewrites Host. Need to verify DNS resolution points to the VPCE IPs and that those hosts bypass the corporate proxy for the private DNS name.
anya: Repro steps to ask customer: 1) dig +short api.redwood.internal (their private DNS for our endpoint) -> should return VPCE IP(s). 2) curl -vk https://api.redwood.internal/health (from affected host) and paste output. 3) tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/t.pcap port 443 host <VPCE_IP> and capture ClientHello to inspect SNI.
customer-engineer: Pasting curl from an affected host:
```
$ curl -vk https://api.redwood.internal/health
*   Trying 10.10.5.23:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.10.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: proxy.local.internal
* SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.local.internal' does not match 'api.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.local.internal' does not match 'api.redwood.internal'
```
That output suggests proxy is terminating TLS and presenting its cert.
sam: Exactly. Two ways to fix short-term: 1) Bypass the proxy for api.redwood.internal (add proxy-bypass rules or PAC change), OR 2) ensure the proxy supports TLS passthrough for that host (no MITM). Also confirm private DNS is enabled on the VPCE so the name resolves to the interface IPs rather than public IPs.
mike: Also check route table(s) for the affected subnets: if some subnets still route 0.0.0.0/0 through corporate gateway, traffic may hairpin and hit the proxy. Use `ip route` / `route -n` on host. Confirm that source routing isn't asymmetric — reply packets need to come back through the VPCE path.
jordan: FYI we’ve seen customers forget to add the VPCE IP range to the proxy allowlist. If proxy rewrites Host header or injects auth, our servers will reject or respond with 401. For interface endpoints, ensure Security Group outbound rules allow ephemeral ports and inbound from the endpoint network.
customer-engineer: We ran tcpdump and extracted TLS ClientHello: SNI shows "proxy.local.internal" instead of "api.redwood.internal". After forcing the host to use NAT-GW (bypassing proxy) and re-running curl, we get 200 OK. So bypass fixed it.
anya: Great root cause. Follow-ups for customer: - Add proxy bypass for api.redwood.internal (or the VPCE IP range) - Enable Private DNS on the VPCE so the hostname resolves internally - Verify per-subnet route tables point to NAT/AZ-specific egress where appropriate - Ensure SGs on the endpoint allow host ephemeral outbound ports and 443 ingress from their VPC.
mike: For our docs: add a short checklist for on-prem/corporate-proxy scenarios: how to validate SNI via tcpdump, curl --resolve to test bypass, and common proxy signs (proxy cert subjects, Proxy-Authorization headers, Host rewrite). I'll draft a KB.
infra-bot: ticket #12345 assigned to eng-infra
ori: Customer will implement proxy-bypass and confirm tomorrow. Marking as a P1 until confirmed.
jordan: If they can't bypass, alternative is to use our Private deployment (within their VPC) or set up a dedicated peering route that avoids corporate proxy hops. But bypass is simplest.
anya: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the customer KB and close once verified. :thumbsup:
